```text
# #4674: Patch: deeper card stats, P1, the patch bar's arrows follow its tabs
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

Part of #4670. Part **P1**, its own pull request on `main`. It needs no other part.

Read first: R1973002, R3324000 and R3324001, `apps/web/src/stats/patches.ts` (`offeredPatches`, `neighbours`), and the patch bar in `apps/web/src/routes/stats.tsx` (`statsTestid.patchBar`, `patchPrevious`, `patchNext`).

## Why

The patch tabs read newest first, left to right. The arrows run the other way:
- **←** (`patchPrevious`) steps to an older patch;
- **→** (`patchNext`) steps to a newer one.

So pressing the right arrow, toward the older tabs, moves left, to a newer patch. The owner found this confusing and asked for the arrows to follow the tabs.

## Build

- The **right** arrow steps one patch **older**, toward the tabs on its side. It is disabled on the oldest patch the page lists.
- The **left** arrow steps one patch **newer**, toward the current patch. It is disabled on the newest.
- Their names say which way they go, as "Older patch (v0.6.9)" and "Newer patch (v0.6.11)", in the `aria-label` and the `title`. "Previous" and "Next" are ambiguous here. Translate them as the page's other strings are (`i18n`).
- Keep the test ids' meaning tied to direction, not side, so the e2e helpers (`e2e/cypress/support/stats.ts`, `visitStatsFigures`) keep working. If a test id must change, change its callers in the same pull request.
- Arrow keys inside the patch tabs, if the Segmented handles them, keep moving along the tabs as drawn.

Before and after, look at the patch bar with the `ui-walkthrough` skill at 1280×720 and 390×844, with the E2E server (`e2e/README.md`), and say in the pull request what you saw.

## Done when

- `apps/web/src/stats/patches.test.ts` and `apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx` cover each arrow's direction, its disabled end and its label.
- Specs 46 and 47 and any spec that steps patches stay green.
- A ruling in this issue's block amends R3324000's arrows, with its test and `spec/pending/<issue>.md` (rule 3), and §9.11's "Patches on `/stats`" bullet says which way each arrow goes.


---
```
